Atmosphere started at ~1 atm, with pressure increasing and O2% dropping due to vitiation.

PSI-23-20170.summary: This experiment tested spherical porous-burner diffusion flames using ethylene fuel diluted with helium in microgravity on the International Space Station. The tests were conducted in atmospheres ranging from approximately 21% to 30% oxygen at roughly 1 atm pressure. The outcome resulted in 20 flames being ignited.
PSI-23-20170.relevance_reason: The test provides useful related evidence involving gas fuels, helium dilution, and flammability limits in microgravity.

PSI-23-20176.summary: This experiment tested spherical porous-burner diffusion flames using helium-diluted ethylene fuel in microgravity aboard the International Space Station. The tests were conducted in oxygen concentrations ranging from approximately 21% to 30% under an atmosphere of about 1 atm. A total of 23 flames ignited during the trials.
PSI-23-20176.relevance_reason: It provides useful related evidence involving gas fuel flammability limits and behavior with helium added as a diluent.
